references.text: The same expression is used earlier in Balaam's prophecy, where he describes himself as one who hears God's words and sees the vision of the Almighty.
Melchizedek uses the title 'God Most High' (El Elyon), the same title that Balaam uses to describe God.
The psalm uses the titles 'Most High' (Elyon) and 'Almighty' (Shaddai) together, just as in Balaam's prophecy.
God reveals himself as 'El Shaddai' (the Almighty) to Abraham, the same title that Balaam uses.
Ezekiel describes his visions as 'visions of God,' similar to Balaam's description of seeing the vision of the Almighty.
Daniel falls with his face to the ground during his vision, similar to Balaam's description of falling down with open eyes.
Daniel describes a state in which he falls into a deep sleep with his face to the ground while receiving revelation.
John falls as if dead when he sees Christ in his glory, similar to Balaam's experience of falling down under divine revelation.
Paul describes a rapture in which he sees the Lord, an experience of divine vision similar to Balaam's.
